findings: Both emitted concepts are owned by party and describe the capacity/role of a party on an IP application; the two dimensions are kept separate as the group purpose requires, so applicant, patentee and agent are not collapsed.

Enum mapping is defensible: enumerated publisher values map to themselves, and the default 'other' is only reachable when the source value is present (when-guard on present), so 'other' never stands in for a blank. Held-out example ordinal 15708 shows raw 'licensee' -> 'other', consistent with the stated definition.

Held-out validation shows 120/120 source-present and 120/120 emitted for each field with 0.0 error rate of present; coverage is honestly bounded to the 25,000-record prefix cohort and no population claim is made.

Grain, identity cautions and unmapped reasons are consistent with the source notes: party_id is not a company number, abn is sparse, party_name is free text, application_number is scoped by ip_right_type, and effective dates are party-activity validity, not incorporation or grant dates.

The mapping does not assert ownership, enforceability, legal form or incorporation from role, name or ABN; the agent row (ordinal 39) is emitted as role 'agent'/'applicant_agent' without any ownership claim.
Unmapped entries for address, validity, identity and party_type columns are correctly scoped out of this group rather than coerced into role values.
The quality note explicitly disclaims semantic truth and useful coverage; the technical gate pass is not presented as human approval or semantic validation.
semantic_risks: 'other' is a lossy bucket: distinct publisher categories (e.g. licensee, mortgagee-adjacent categories) collapse into one value, so downstream consumers cannot distinguish them; this is a coverage/utility limitation, not a semantic error, given the stated definition.

The 'unknown' enum value is declared but unreachable under the present-guard; this is consistent with declining blanks rather than coercing them, but the value is effectively dead in this mapping and should not be read as evidence that blanks were classified.

Role category and role are publisher-supplied labels; a party recorded as 'applicant' is not proof of current ownership or enforceability, and any downstream join to right status must not treat these as such.
Prefix-cohort bias means role distribution frequencies are not representative of the full archive; no frequency or share claims should be derived.
checked_reuse: ext.contact.* — rejected: different owner (contact channels) and different meaning; reuse would change owner and meaning.
ext.licence.* / ext.licence.category — rejected: describes a licence authorisation held by a business, a different owner and meaning; would misstate the party-application role fact.
No existing shortlisted concept describes a party's capacity or specific role on an IP application, so new party-owned concepts are justified.
response.rationale: The two proposed concepts are party-owned, semantically distinct dimensions (broad role category vs specific role label) that match the group purpose of not collapsing applicant, patentee and agent roles. Enum handling is sound: enumerated values map identically, and the default 'other' is only reachable for present-but-unenumerated source values, with blanks declined rather than coerced. Held-out validation shows full coverage of present values with zero error rate of present, and the group honestly bounds itself to a prefix cohort without population claims. Identity, date and legal-form cautions are respected: no ownership, enforceability, incorporation or legal-form inference is made from role, name or ABN. No blocking semantic, ownership, unit, date or provenance defect was found in the emitted claims; the noted risks are utility/interpretation limitations rather than incorrect assertions.
